text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Lack of funds delays completion of motorway between capital city and Black Sea port of Constanta. It costs $4.5 million to build one kilometre of road.
- National Bank licensed new commercial bank Astra located in Transylvanian city of Brasov.
AZI
- Bucharest stock exchange has no trading sessions this week as it installs new software. Bourse said another seven companies applied for listing.
LIBERTATEA
- Capital market regulator CNVM approved norms for operation of registry and settlement company to back up over-the-counter market due to start trading soon.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Beer brewer Bere Rahova SA awaits investor to buy 40 percent stake which its main stockholder State Ownership Fund plans to sell for cash under mass selloff scheme.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- World Bank to give Romania $24 million loan for road rehabilitation.
- Romania and Yugoslavia signed accords on cooperation in tourism, agriculture and food industry.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romanian police discovered four tonnes of hashish hidden in a train loaded with furniture bound for Moscov.
- Romania will be in first wave of former East European countries to join NATO, Romanian envoy to Washington Mircea Geoana said.
ADEVARUL
- President Ion Iliescu said he accepts to run in the November 3 parliamentary elections also on the list of ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) for lower Chamber of Deputies.
- France's Pasteur Institute confirms meningitis epidemic in Romania was spread by moskitoes.
- Emil Constantinescu, presidential candidate of opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc said CDR would form a coalition government after the November 3 polls.
- Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu to run for upper house of Senate on list of ruling PDSR.
DIMINEATA
- Newspaper publishes excerpts from electoral programme of ruling PDSR.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Bucharest is besieged by baggers, street children and stray dogs, the paper says.

- Supreme court of justice to start on October 7 trial of three army officers accused of "massacre" in December 1989, when 50 soldiers were killed and other 13 were wounded near the Otopeni international airport.
ZIUA
- Melescanu to have talks with his Ukrainien counterpart Genadi Udovenko over basic treaty between the two countries during a visit to New York.
COTIDIANUL

- Interviews with Valentin Gabrielescu, opposition National Peasant Party senator and Sergiu Nicolaescu, ruling PDSR senator over report on December 1989 revolt. The two, members of a parliamentary commision investigating the 1989 events, have different opinions on those events. ($=3,227 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
